newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Report says Singapore Q1 property prices ease - TV.
newsitem.headline: Report says Singapore Q1 property prices ease - TV.

text.p: Residential property prices eased further in the first quarter of 1997 according to the latest Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) figures reported by state television on Friday.
"Market watchers say the dip is within expectations and more softening is expected," the television report said.

Condominium prices dropped 5.8 percent in the first quarter compared to a one percent fall in the previous quarter, while landed properties slipped 1.3 percent -- an improvement on the 4.4 percent previously, the report said.
Prices of detached houses rose by 2.6 percent while prices of terraced and semi-detached homes fell by 4.0 percent and 2.6 percent respectively.
"There are falling rentals and this made investors very cautious," the report quoted an analyst as saying.
Commercial property prices meanwhile fell 4.3 percent compared with 2.0 percent in the previous quarter, although industrial property prices rose 4.3 percent against a previous 0.5 percent fall.
Prices of flatted factories rose by 5.5 percent, but warehouses dropped 3.2 percent.
